item.title: Jamie Foxx Returns To The Boxing Corner As Netflix Dates Fight For ’84
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jamie Foxx stars as the coach rebuilding the U.S. Olympic boxing team in Fight for '84, streaming February 19 on Netflix.
item.content:encoded:
Jamie Foxx will take a team of American boxers from a national tragedy to the Los Angeles Olympics in Fight for ’84. Netflix set a February 19, 2027 premiere for the drama and shared a first look at Foxx as the coach charged with rebuilding the U.S. team.

Foxx stars in and produces the movie, which opens in the aftermath of a 1980 plane crash that killed members of the U.S. boxing delegation. The film follows the coach as he assembles a new squad and prepares it to compete at the 1984 Summer Games.

The real team won 11 medals in Los Angeles, nine of them gold, according to USA Boxing’s Olympic results. Mark Breland, Pernell Whitaker and Henry Tillman were among the Americans who won their weight classes, while Evander Holyfield took bronze. Tillman is also an executive producer on the film.

Director Andrés Baiz, whose Netflix work includes Griselda and Narcos, said the story drew him in for reasons that had little to do with the medal count.

“It’s a story about second chances, about rebuilding after loss, and about finding strength through connection,” he told Tudum. Baiz also singled out Foxx’s involvement on both sides of the camera, calling the chance to work with him “incredibly exciting.”

Andrea Berloff, who co-wrote Straight Outta Compton, wrote the script with John Gatins and White Boy Rick co-writer Andy Weiss. Netflix’s cast guide lists Malachi Beasley, Shea Whigham and Algee Smith, who played Ralph Tresvant in The New Edition Story.

Foxx already played one of boxing’s best-known corner men as Drew “Bundini” Brown opposite Will Smith in Ali. His work in music includes the T-Pain collaboration “Blame It,” which won a Grammy in 2010 for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals.

Fight for ’84 is a separate project from the horror series Foxx and his daughter Corinne have in development through their deal with Fox. It also puts him back at Netflix after Back in Action, the 2025 comedy he starred in with Cameron Diaz.

This time, Foxx’s job in the ring is to get a new team ready before the Games come home.

item.title: Don Toliver Moves Wembley Show To December After Manchester Evacuation
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Don Toliver's Wembley show moves to December 14 after the Manchester evacuation. The O2 show is now set for December 15.
item.content:encoded:
Don Toliver will play London’s OVO Arena Wembley on December 14 instead of November 24.

An evacuation cut short his Manchester set two nights before he was due at Wembley.

The promoter said the crew couldn’t get the production equipment from Manchester’s Co-op Live to London in time.

“All tickets remain valid for the new date,” the promoter said in a statement posted by Wembley.

Doors open at 6:30 p.m. local time.

The Wembley date now falls the night before Toliver’s other London concert.

His November 23 appearance at The O2 had already moved to December 15, and tickets for that night will also carry over.

For the people who had to leave the Manchester show on November 22, the promoter is offering a full refund.

Ticket holders won’t have to apply to get their money back.

More than 12,000 people left Co-op Live after reports of an unknown substance in the arena, Greater Manchester Police said.

Of the 89 people who showed symptoms, one woman went to Manchester Royal Infirmary for treatment.

The other 88 were decontaminated at the scene and then taken to nearby Etihad Stadium.

Police ended the major incident response at 4 a.m. Monday but kept the investigation open.

Officers collected items from the arena for testing and said they had found no evidence of a wider threat to the public.

Toliver addressed the evacuation on Instagram when he announced the first London postponement, sending his prayers to those hurt in Manchester.

item.title: GloRilla Lands First Acting Role In Deon Taylor’s Horror Thriller
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: GloRilla makes her acting debut in Deon Taylor's Don't Open the Door, a horror thriller starring Armani Greer and Tyrese Gibson.
item.content:encoded:
GloRilla is making her acting debut in Don’t Open the Door, a horror thriller written and directed by Deon Taylor, who directed The Intruder.

The Memphis rapper is joining a cast led by Armani Greer that also includes Tyrese Gibson, Variety reported.

Taylor confirmed the two castings but hasn’t revealed who GloRilla will play.

“Pairing Armani with GloRilla in her acting debut gave us something audiences haven’t seen before,” he told Variety.

Greer, who played Jasmine in Why Did I Get Married Again?, will play the central role. Her other screen work includes The Drop: A Snowfall Saga and the Atlanta-set crime drama The Waterboyz.

Taylor and producer Roxanne Avent Taylor are making the movie through their independent studio, Hidden Empire Film Group.

Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Cam Heyward is producing through Iron 97 Productions, alongside Shannon McIntosh, whose credits include Once Upon a Time in Hollywood and The Hateful Eight.

The filmmakers haven’t released a plot summary, but they told Variety the story “focuses on real-world trauma.”

That leaves the nature of the threat and the characters’ relationship under wraps. The studio also plans to build a larger world around the film, taking its cues from graphic novels. The trade reported that filming is underway in Mississippi.

Gibson isn’t the only familiar face in the cast.

Sinners actor Omar Benson Miller joins him, along with The Conjuring‘s Ron Livingston and Beverly D’Angelo from the National Lampoon’s Vacation movies. Maxime Alexandre, who shot The Nun and Annabelle: Creation, is the cinematographer.

It’s a different kind of set for GloRilla, who broke out with “F.N.F. (Let’s Go)” before releasing her debut album, Glorious, in 2024.

She and Sexyy Red recently reunited on “Jiggly Bow Bow” after teaming up on “Whatchu Kno About Me” and appearing together on Tyler, The Creator’s “Sticky.”

Taylor has already worked across horror and comedy with Meet the Blacks, and made the police thriller Black and Blue, which also starred Gibson. For Don’t Open the Door, the writer-director is giving Greer the lead and putting a rapper used to performing as herself into her first acting role.

No release date has been announced.

item.title: Cardi B Admits She Doubted Her Ear After Seven Years Between Albums
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cardi B says seven years between albums made her question her own taste before Am I the Drama? returned her to No. 1.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B wasn’t sure she could still hear a hit when she was making Am I the Drama?

The Bronx rapper had spent seven years between albums, and she said in an interview with Billboard Canada that the wait made her question whether her instincts were still any good.

She’d already scored hits with “WAP” and “Up” between Invasion of Privacy and her second album. But Cardi described a different test in putting a whole record in front of listeners: finding out whether they heard the same thing she did.

She needed to find out “if I still got that ear, if I still got that in me,” she told the magazine.

She compared it to baking a cake that everyone close to you loves, then finding out whether anybody would actually pay for a slice. If it doesn’t sell, she said, you start questioning what you thought you knew.

Am I the Drama? answered one of those questions when it debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in September 2025. Cardi still had another test ahead. She’d never headlined a tour, and the Little Miss Drama show called for more than 35 songs a night, plus choreography.

“The job was not done,” she said of the period after the album dropped. She started the tour three months after having her fourth child.

The experience also meant finding out whether she could handle a two-hour show, not just whether she could make a record people wanted to play.

On the road, Cardi said fans came up to her in tears and told her how her music had helped them through hard stretches.

She could relate: During rough moments, she said, she plays whole albums on repeat, turning to singers such as Mariah the Scientist, Beyoncé, Rihanna and Aretha Franklin.

Billboard Canada had already named her its first Global Woman of the Year, with the ceremony set for November 24 in Toronto.

Now it’s the feeling she gets onstage, Cardi said, that keeps pulling her back.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Disney Sued Over Sha Gz Beat In ESPN Promos
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: LAA Music and Zac Hiller say ESPN, Hulu, Disney Parks and FX used three works without licenses in seven promotional videos.
item.content:encoded:
The Walt Disney Company faces a federal copyright lawsuit over seven promotional videos, including ESPN clips that allegedly used the beat behind Sha Gz‘s “New Opp.”

Music L.A.A. and its owner, Zac Hiller, filed the complaint Tuesday in Michigan, accusing Disney of using three works without permission.

The lawsuit also names up to ten unidentified people or businesses that allegedly helped make or distribute the clips.

The claim over “New Opp” doesn’t cover Sha Gz’s finished recording. LAA says producer Souleyman Ble Gueu, known as Soumadethis, made the original beat and signed over a 50% interest in his rights in June 2025.

The filing says two short ESPN clips used the beat and a third used it through “Pink Dreads,” a song at the center of a separate lawsuit involving DDG.

“The beat is not background noise in these videos. It is the soundtrack,” the complaint says of the two shorter clips.

According to the filing, Disney’s lawyers attributed those posts to an unnamed Dutch company and said it had agreed to cover ESPN’s legal liability for them.

The suit also singles out an Abbott Elementary promotion that actor Janelle James posted on TikTok to direct viewers to Hulu.

The plaintiffs say the clip used “Gang Gang,” a composition they credit to Trayvon Jackson, and had drawn about 481,700 likes by October 3. They allege Disney helped arrange or promote the video, but the complaint does not name James as a defendant.

The third work, Jackson’s “Take It Off (Lights Off)” beat, allegedly appeared in two TikToks featuring Disney’s Animal Kingdom and an Instagram post promoting FX’s The Drop.

The complaint says the two TikTok creators got Disney products, services or experiences through its influencer program.

“Instead, after Plaintiffs’ notices, all seven videos came down,” the complaint says in describing the removals.

The plaintiffs say they began notifying Disney in August and that the company never produced a license. Disney had not filed an answer in the docket at the time of review.

The plaintiffs want a jury trial and an order barring further unlicensed use. They seek lost licensing fees and attributable profits or, alternatively, up to $150,000 per work if they establish willful infringement and statutory damages are available.

item.title: Drake Confirms Texas’ Brenham Saddle Shop Will Reopen In 2027
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Drake says the historic Brenham Saddle Shop will reopen in 2027 after 65 years in business and a closure that began in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
Drake gave a shuttered Texas Western wear shop a new timetable, telling followers that the Brenham Saddle Shop will be ready for customers in 2027.

The Toronto rapper shared a video from the store on his Instagram Story, Holler reported on Tuesday, November 24. “We will be ready for you 2027…Opening date TBA…Come visit us,” he wrote.

The post puts a year on the comeback without giving shoppers a date to circle. Earlier this year, the shop’s account had pointed to a fall reopening, according to local station KBTX. The 2027 update moves that estimate into next year.

William Schmidt opened the first Brenham Saddle Shop downtown in 1960. It moved to Highway 290 in 1963 and spent decades selling Western clothing, hats and equestrian equipment. His great-grandson, Sage Nutt, told KBTX that country singers had stopped by in the 1970s and 1980s. The shop closed in April 2025 after 65 years.

Trademark paperwork surfaced before the new timetable did. KBTX reported that an earlier application by ADG Vanguard IP LLC went dead. The station said the active application, filed through Austin attorney Robert Kleinman, was approved in November 2025.

As AllHipHop reported in July, the filing led to questions about what role Drake might play in the revival. His new post publicly links him to the reopening plans, but its ownership remains unclear.

AllHipHop’s July report also noted that the family behind the business had described the shutdown as temporary. When the shop closed, Nutt told KBTX he hoped the next operator would preserve what his family built. “I’m very excited for any sort of person that comes in and decides to do something with this place,” he said.

Drake already has ties to the area. He bought a ranch near Brenham, at the former Inn at Dos Brisas. KBTX reported that Drake had been a frequent visitor since buying property in Washington County. One of the station’s reporters shared a photo of him at the shop in December 2024, before the business closed.

The store’s own post advertised Western apparel and signaled that the shop was preparing to return. The shop has not announced when it will start taking customers.

item.title: 2 Chainz Says He Broke His Ribs In Head-On Cybertruck Crash
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: 2 Chainz says he's resting with broken ribs after a car swerved to avoid an opossum and hit his Cybertruck head-on.
item.content:encoded:
2 Chainz says he broke his ribs in a head-on crash in his Tesla Cybertruck. The Atlanta rapper shared the news Tuesday, November 24. He said the other driver swerved to miss an opossum and hit him instead.

He said he was on a two-way road in his orange Cybertruck when the other car came at him. In his Instagram post, he thanked fans for checking on him.

“A lot of calls and concern on my well being, i appreciate everyone who reaching out , im good , just resting with broke ribs , no I wasn’t drinking,smoking ,sleeping or on auto pilot , the other driver dodged a possum and hit me head on , smh , hope that answers all of your questions , Blessed
4h

,” 2 Chainz wrote.

The first clip he shared showed the truck in the grass by the road after dark. The footage ran in an Instagram Story posted Monday, November 23. Damage was visible near the front wheel, with light-colored debris on the ground. The truck was not moving in the clip.

2 Chainz also went to the hospital after a crash in Miami on December 9, 2023. Florida Highway Patrol told CBS News Miami that three vehicles crashed on State Road 112 near Northwest 22nd Avenue.

Miami Fire Rescue said he was the only one taken to the hospital. He posted from an ambulance at that time and later thanked fans after he got out.

item.title: D’Angelo Approved “Kamikazi” Before His Death, Estate Confirms
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: D'Angelo's estate says he approved the finished recording in November 2024. "Kamikazi" is now out as a standalone single.
item.content:encoded:
D’Angelo approved the finished version of “Kamikazi” for Grand Theft Auto VI nearly a year before he died, his estate said. The song, a collaboration with Slingbaum, came out as a standalone RCA single Monday, November 23, after debuting on the game’s radio.

His brother Luther Archer Jr. said D’Angelo signed off on the version listeners are hearing now. “Michael approved this track in its current form in November of 2024 to be released as part of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Archer said in a statement.

The finished track grew out of sessions with D’Angelo, Slingbaum and longtime engineer Ben Kane. Kane told Vulture that he and D’Angelo recorded an early sketch and put it aside.

The singer came back to it in November 2024 to pitch it to Rockstar’s soundtrack team, bringing Slingbaum in to finish it. “This is one of very few things that he had explicitly approved to be released,” Kane said.

D’Angelo spoke about adding guitar to his work and looking back on Voodoo in a conversation with Nelson George at the Brooklyn Museum.

Slingbaum suggested recording two drum parts, according to Kane. Yussef Dayes and the late James Gadson played against the same beat D’Angelo had programmed, recording from different studios. Dayes comes through on the left and Gadson from the right. Nick Hakim brought together several of the backing singers, including Jermaine Holmes, keiyaA and June McDoom.

The session reunited two artists who worked together on “Behoove,” a song from Slingbaum’s 2020 vinyl release that also featured Erykah Badu. Gilles Peterson played that track on BBC Radio 6 Music. His in-game station, Worldwide FM, is where players first heard “Kamikazi.”

The new single also follows a posthumous guest appearance on “This Woman,” released by Busta Rhymes and J Dilla in August. D’Angelo and Slingbaum are billed together on “Kamikazi.”

It is D’Angelo’s second song for Rockstar. Players heard “Unshaken” in Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018 before it reached streaming in January 2019. Archer told Vulture that he and his brother used to play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City together more than any other game in the series.

item.title: Flavor Flav Joins Lakers Forward For Late-Night Shooting Workout
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Flavor Flav rebounded for Lakers forward Sandro Mamukelashvili in a late-night workout after a tough shooting stretch.
item.content:encoded:
Flavor Flav went from cheering on Sandro Mamukelashvili to chasing down his rebounds at the Lakers’ practice facility. The Public Enemy rapper joined his friend for an after-hours shooting workout after the forward went 1-for-10 against the Utah Jazz.

Mamukelashvili told reporters he headed to the facility straight from the game, still in his shorts. He had made just four of 26 shots over three games and wanted to get back on a court instead of carrying that last performance home with him.

In that game, he finished with six points and three rebounds, making all four free throws but missing all four three-point attempts. Utah won 109-97.

Flav had been at the game and came along. The forward told reporters that his friend, usually the loudest person in the room, took one look at how seriously he was shooting and dialed back the volume.

“It was cool actually, he was out there trying to rebound,” Mamukelashvili said. “So, shoutout to him for coming to the gym. It was cool.”

ESPN’s Dave McMenamin shared a video of Mamukelashvili describing the workout and reported that he shot until 2:30 A.M. The forward said seeing Kobe Bryant’s numbers lit up on the wall made him think about how often even the greats have had to work through a bad stretch.

The pair’s friendship dates back to summer league in 2021, when Mamukelashvili was entering the NBA. The two met through his financial adviser, and they’ve since gone to Yankees games together, the New York Post reported.

The Lakers even asked Mamukelashvili about Flav for an official introduction to fans after he joined the team. The forward was born in New York, grew up in Tbilisi, Georgia, and played for Milwaukee, San Antonio, and Toronto before landing in Los Angeles.

Flav’s sports support usually puts him in the stands or online. Last month, he wrote a mock work excuse for WNBA fans who wanted to catch a Finals game during the workday.

Mamukelashvili shot 4-for-8 for nine points against Sacramento on Friday, though he was still looking for his next made three-pointer.

item.title: Moneybagg Yo Brings Thanksgiving Groceries To 200 Memphis Families
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Moneybagg Yo helped feed about 200 Memphis families at his Thanksgiving giveaway, with the city and county mayors pitching in.
item.content:encoded:
Moneybagg Yo brought Thanksgiving groceries to about 200 Memphis families on Monday, November 23, with the city’s mayor and the county mayor helping hand them out.

The Memphis rapper and his label, NLess Entertainment, held the Bagg’s Table Thanksgiving Giveback at the Memphis Sports and Events Center in Liberty Park.

Families picked up turkeys, fresh produce and other groceries. Memphis Mayor Paul Young and Shelby County Mayor Mickell Lowery both helped distribute the food, Action News 5 reported from the event.

“Look at the smiles on the people’s faces,” Young told the station. He said the rapper is putting Memphis on the map nationally through Hip-Hop while still looking out for the people in his hometown. “We know a lot of families are struggling right now,” Lowery told the station.

“This is what this season is about,” Moneybagg Yo said, according to The Daily Memphian. “This is the season for no hate.”

The American Heart Association gave an educational presentation. Families could also get a photo with Moneybagg Yo. NLess general manager Kemario Brown told Action News 5 that the rapper came back to Memphis because families there needed the help.

This year’s giveaway took place at a different location from the one Moneybagg Yo helped organize last Thanksgiving. In 2025, families lined up outside the former Crystal Palace skating rink in Southwest Memphis, where his mother’s Larger Than L.I.F.E. Foundation and Memphis rapper IME Casino worked with him to give out food and household supplies.

That Thanksgiving effort was followed by a Christmas toy drive that Moneybagg Yo said he wanted to make an annual event. In January, he gave $20,000 to the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Youth Advocacy Program to help students who are raising children stay in school. He said the work hit close to home because his mother raised him when she was a teenager.

Moneybagg Yo had also used his platform to support literacy in Memphis well before those events. In 2023, the Shelby County mayor’s office said he gave away $1,000 in gifts at a grandparents’ literacy breakfast, where he served as a literacy ambassador.

Another Memphis rapper is following with her own Thanksgiving event: GloRilla is set to give away turkeys on Tuesday, November 24, at Smackers on South Highland Street.
